title: Underground Streets and Feteasca Neagră: A Week Through Codru and Ștefan Vodă
subRegion: Chișinău, the Codru hills, Ștefan Vodă and the southern Valul lui Traian

bestPeriod.window: the last ten days of September through the first weekend of October (harvest, then Ziua Națională a Vinului)
bestPeriod.avoid: July–early August (35 °C on the Bugeac steppe, cellars are the only cool place) and January–March (many small domains close their tasting rooms)

accommodation.note: €260–€480 (€37–€69/night; Chișinău mid-range plus two nights at a wine estate)

transport.note: €330–€480 (driver-guide with car, 5 working days, €65–€95/day — mandatory, see below)

hook: Moldova is the only wine country where you tour two of the cellars by car, windows down, headlights on, past street signs that read *Cabernet* and *Feteasca*. Above ground it is quieter than that sounds: low Codru hills of walnut and vine, villages of blue-painted gates, and a capital that eats plăcinte at 08:00. Come in the last week of September and you will smell fermentation from the road. It suits drinkers who want producers, not pageantry.

snapshot.Best period: Late September–October; the first weekend of October for Wine Day
snapshot.Start / End: Chișinău → Chișinău (radial, with two nights out at Purcari and Butuceni)

itinerary.title: Chișinău, Landing and the First Glass
itinerary.morning: Land at KIV, drop bags, and orient on Bulevardul Ștefan cel Mare — the Arcul de Triumf, the Catedrala Nașterea Domnului with its free-standing belfry, the Ștefan cel Mare monument at the park gate. Twenty minutes fixes the city's grid in your head.
itinerary.afternoon: **Piața Centrală** for the food groundwork: barrels of *must* in season, sheep's brânză, walnuts, dried plums, and the divin counter. Then late plăcinte at **La Plăcinte** on Ștefan cel Mare.
itinerary.evening: A structured by-the-glass flight at **Carpe Diem**, the city's serious wine bar — ask for Viorica, then a Rara Neagră, then a Fetească Neagră, in that order [VERIFY: current hours and address]. Dinner at **Vatra Neamului** for zeamă and mămăligă.

itinerary.title: The Two Underground Cities
itinerary.morning: North to **Cricova**. The tour runs by electric train through galleries quarried for limestone and converted to wine storage in the 1950s; it holds 12–14 °C, so bring a jacket even in September. Finish in the tasting rooms on the traditional-method sparkling.
itinerary.afternoon: South through Chișinău to **Mileștii Mici**, driven along the underground avenues past the *Golden Collection* to a tasting hall; the scale, not the wine list, is the point. Allow an hour of city traffic between the two.
itinerary.evening: Eat lightly — **Propaganda Cafe**, or a bowl of zeamă near Parcul Catedralei. Two big lunches are coming.

itinerary.title: East to the Dniester: Bulboaca and Purcari
itinerary.morning: Out on the R30 to **Castel Mimi** at Bulboaca, 35 km east. Tour the restored 1893 cellar, then taste the Codru whites; with its garden, spa and restaurant this is the one stop here that works for a non-drinker.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue southeast to **Château Purcari**, 60 km on, for the **Negru de Purcari** vertical: Cabernet Sauvignon with Saperavi and Rara Neagră in French oak, and the 1878 Paris story told properly.
itinerary.evening: Stay at the **Purcari Wine Resort** — villas on the estate lake. Dinner is estate cooking with estate wine, which is exactly the point of driving this far [VERIFY: current villa rates and restaurant hours].

itinerary.title: Ștefan Vodă Proper: Crocmaz and the Way Home
itinerary.morning: Walk the Purcari vineyard blocks before breakfast — the Dniester valley light at 07:30 is the photograph of the week. Then 20 km to **Et Cetera** at Crocmaz, the Luchianov brothers' domain: small, precise, and the best place in the country to understand Rara Neagră on its own.
itinerary.afternoon: Loop back northwest to **Asconi** at Puhăceni for a courtyard lunch — grilled meats, mămăligă, house Fetească Neagră — in the reconstructed village-street setting the estate built around its cellar.
itinerary.evening: Into Chișinău by early evening: sarmale and a glass of Fetească Regală somewhere unambitious. The week's second half is the harder driving.

itinerary.title: Orheiul Vechi, the Non-Wine Day
itinerary.morning: North on the R14 to **Orheiul Vechi**, 55 km. Park at Butuceni and walk up the limestone promontory above the meander of the Răut to the **cave monastery** — a 13th-century hermitage cut into the cliff, with a bell tower on the ridge above and the church of the Ascension beside it. Cover shoulders; it is an active place of prayer.
itinerary.afternoon: Lunch in **Butuceni** — plăcinte, chicken zeamă, house wine from a plastic bottle, the honest other half of Moldovan wine culture. Then 18 km to **Chateau Vartely** above **Orhei**, tasting on the terrace.
itinerary.evening: Stay in a Butuceni guesthouse. No light pollution, and the promontory at dusk is worth walking twice.

itinerary.title: South to Valul lui Traian: Tigheci and Cimișlia
itinerary.morning: The long day. Drive south from Chișinău through Hîncești and Leova toward the **Tigheci** hills for **Fautor** — the most convincing modern estate in the south, and the reference point for Moldovan Viorica and for late-harvest whites.
itinerary.afternoon: East across the Valul lui Traian earthwork toward Cimișlia for **Gitana**, whose reds are the broad, sun-driven counterweight to everything you drank in Codru. Ask to taste Rara Neagră from both zones back to back if the cellar will pour it.
itinerary.evening: Back in Chișinău around 19:00: a Bardar XO or Călărași divin, then an early night [VERIFY: current Fautor and Gitana visitor days].

itinerary.title: Codru Garagistes and Wine Day
itinerary.morning: Small Codru producers within 40 km of the capital: **Equinox**, **Novak**, **Atu Winery**. Two of the three in a morning is realistic; all three is not. Here you meet the winemaker, not a guide.
itinerary.afternoon: If the trip is timed to the **first weekend of October**, this is **Ziua Națională a Vinului** — a hundred-odd producers pouring in Piața Marii Adunări Naționale. Buy the glass, walk the rows, find the four-hectare estates you will never see abroad.
itinerary.evening: Last supper at **Gustar** or back at **Carpe Diem**, then Piața Centrală in the morning for divin and walnuts to carry home. Duty-free allowances into the EU are two litres of wine and one of spirits per adult [VERIFY: current EU allowance for Moldova].

accommodationStrategy.name: Nobil Luxury Boutique Hotel
accommodationStrategy.description: central but off the Ștefan cel Mare noise line, walkable to Carpe Diem and Piața Centrală, breakfast early enough for a 07:30 departure.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 3–4 weeks direct; four months for the Wine Day weekend, when the city sells out.

accommodationStrategy.name: Purcari Wine Resort
accommodationStrategy.description: it removes the worst decision on this itinerary — driving 120 km back to Chișinău after a Negru de Purcari vertical. Lakeside villas, estate restaurant, vines at the door.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 4–8 weeks through the château, bundled with the tasting.

accommodationStrategy.name: Butuceni Eco-Resort
accommodationStrategy.description: restored *casa mare* rooms with clay stoves, a kitchen doing zeamă and plăcinte, five minutes from the cave monastery path.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 2–3 weeks ahead; ask whether dinner is included [VERIFY: current rates and dinner arrangement].

logistics.connectivity: Moldova is not in EU roaming. Buy a local SIM or eSIM (Orange, Moldcell) at the airport; 4G is good on main roads, patchy in the Tigheci hills.
logistics.emergency: 112 nationwide, English is not guaranteed. Carry your driver-guide's number and your accommodation's; rural pharmacies close by 18:00.
logistics.weather: sharply continental. Late September runs 20–27 °C by day, dropping to 8 °C at night in the Codru; October rain turns unsurfaced vineyard tracks to mud within an hour.
logistics.bookingWindows: Mileștii Mici, Cricova, Purcari 1–3 weeks (longer in autumn); Fautor and Et Cetera 1–2 weeks; Castel Mimi, Asconi, Vartely 3–7 days; Chișinău hotels four months for Wine Day.
logistics.money: the leu (MDL), roughly 19–20 to the euro [VERIFY: current rate]. Cards work in Chișinău and at the big estates; carry cash for guesthouses, monastery donations and market stalls. Change at a bank or a *casa de schimb valutar* in town, never at the airport rate.
logistics.transportRules: **Moldova enforces a 0.00 blood-alcohol limit.** No "one glass" tolerance, penalties include vehicle seizure — which is why a hired driver-guide is the structural requirement this itinerary is built around, at €65–€95 a day with car and fuel [VERIFY: current driver-guide day rate]. Self-driving on a non-tasting day: headlights on outside built-up areas year-round, signs Romanian-only.
logistics.permits: no permits for any winery here. Transnistria (the left bank of the Dniester, Tiraspol and Bender) is outside Chișinău's control and hire cars are often contractually barred from entering; this itinerary never crosses. Purcari sits on the right bank, well clear of it.

proTips: Book Cricova at 10:00 and Mileștii Mici at 15:00 on the same day. They sit either side of Chișinău and the afternoon slot dodges the 17:00 traffic.
Take a fleece underground. Both cellars hold 12–14 °C all year and tours run 90 minutes; September T-shirts are misery by the third gallery.
If you can taste only one native, ask for **Rara Neagră** over Fetească Neagră — rarer, lighter, and almost never exported.
Buy *must* roadside between about 20 September and 5 October — unfiltered fermenting juice in reused bottles, drinkable for two days, and the taste of Moldovan autumn.

Time Day 7 to the first Saturday of October. Ziua Națională a Vinului puts a hundred producers on one square for the price of a glass — the fastest way to find domains you would otherwise never locate.
Learn *"Un pahar de vin roșu, vă rog"* and *"Cât costă?"*. Russian works everywhere, but Romanian is noticeably better received in the villages.
Ship rather than carry — Purcari, Castel Mimi and Vartely arrange EU shipping. Six bottles in hold luggage is a false economy once you pay the excess-baggage fee.

raw.Appellations (IGP): **Codru** — the forested central hills around Chișinău, 150–350 m, the coolest zone; whites and mid-weight reds, home of Fetească Albă, Fetească Regală and the aromatic modern crossing **Viorica**. **Ștefan Vodă** — the southeast toward the Dniester and the Black Sea influence; warmer, longer autumns, the classic terroir for **Rara Neagră** and **Fetească Neagră**, the natives that give Negru de Purcari its spine. **Valul lui Traian** — the south, named for the Roman earthwork; the biggest, warmest zone, broad ripe reds around Cimișlia and the Tigheci hills. All three are IGP (*Indicație Geografică Protejată*) [VERIFY: current PDO/IGP labelling practice].
raw.Reservation-only domains — treat as abso: **Mileștii Mici**, **Cricova** and **Château Purcari** must be booked ahead; at the two underground cities walk-ins are effectively impossible, because a tour means a vehicle and a guide allocated to you. Book them 1–3 weeks out by email or web form, longer in harvest month; all three still refuse walk-ins and take reservations by phone or web form only. Budget per person (2026): **Cricova** from 250 MDL (about €13) for the weekday-morning tour alone, 400 MDL with a souvenir bottle, 700 MDL for the tour with a three-wine tasting and 950 MDL for six wines with cheese; **Mileștii Mici** 350 MDL (450 MDL evenings and weekends) for the 50-minute drive-through including the Golden Collection, 800 MDL for the tour with three wines and charcuterie; **Château Purcari** 300 MDL for the château tour alone and 450 MDL for the Classic tasting of four wines, rising to 600–1,000 MDL for the Reserve, Parcela and Academia flights, most of which carry a two- to five-person minimum. **Fautor** (Tigheci) and **Et Cetera** (Crocmaz) are small and also appointment-only. **Castel Mimi**, **Asconi** and **Chateau Vartely** run scheduled tours and a restaurant, so they tolerate short notice — but not on a September Saturday.
raw.Named producers: **Cricova**, 15 km north — 120 km of limestone galleries at 60–80 m depth, streets named after the wines stored along them, traditional-method sparkling. **Mileștii Mici**, 20 km south — the Guinness-record collection, roughly 1.5 million bottles in some 200 km of galleries, around 55 km in use; you are driven through it. **Château Purcari** (1827, Ștefan Vodă) — Negru de Purcari, the Cabernet–Saperavi–Rara Neagră blend whose ancestor took gold at the 1878 Paris Exposition. **Castel Mimi** at Bulboaca — Constantin Mimi's 1893 château, restored, with a serious restaurant. Then **Asconi** (Puhăceni), **Et Cetera** (Crocmaz, the Luchianov brothers), **Fautor** (Tigheci), **Gitana** in the south, **Chateau Vartely** above Orhei, and the small Codru names **Equinox**, **Novak** and **Atu Winery** [VERIFY: current tasting-room days at Equinox, Novak and Atu].
raw.Signature dishes: **plăcinte** (coiled pastry with brânză, cartofi, varză or cherries), **zeamă** (sour chicken-and-noodle broth lifted with borș de tărâțe), **mămăligă cu brânză și smântână** (polenta, sheep's cheese, sour cream — cut with a wooden knife, never metal), **sarmale** in cabbage or vine leaves, **must** (cloudy fermenting juice, roadside for about ten days a year), and **divin**, the aged brandy — Bardar and Călărași Divin are the names.
